result.topic_en: Gauss defines infinite products W(φ,x) and T(φ,x) and expresses them and W² as theta-type cosine/sine series whose coefficients are given via the arithmetic-geometric mean M, with theta series identities.
result.transcription:
Math. 25 \quad 47d/ [-3-] \quad (54)
Designando $\left(\frac{1+2\cos 2\varphi\, xx + x^4}{1+2xx+x^4}\right)\left(\frac{1+2\cos 2\varphi\, x^6 + x^{12}}{1+2x^6+x^{12}}\right)\ldots$ per
$W(\varphi,x)$, erit
1) $W(\varphi,x) = \mathfrak{P}(1+2xx\cos 2\varphi + 2x^8\cos 4\varphi + 2x^{18}\cos 6\varphi +$
$\mathfrak{P} = \frac{1}{1+2xx+2x^8+2x^{18}\ldots} = \sqrt{M\cos v}$

2) $W(\varphi,x)^2 = Q(1+[-2xx-]{+2x+}\cos 2\varphi + 2x^4\cos 4\varphi + 2x^9\cos 6\varphi\ldots$
$+R(1+2x^4\cos 4\varphi + 2x^{16}\cos 8\varphi \ldots)$
$= Q\, W(\varphi, x^{\frac12}) + R\, W(2\varphi, xx)$
$Q = \sin\frac12 v\sqrt{M\cos v} = \frac{2x+2x^9+2x^{25}\ldots}{(1+2xx+2x^8)^2\ldots}$
$R = (\cos\frac12 v - \sin\frac12 v)\sqrt{M\cos v} = \frac{1-2x+2x^4-2x^9\ldots}{(1+2xx+2x^8\ldots)^2}$

Designando
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{M\cos\varphi}}\cdot\sin\varphi\, \frac{1-2\cos 2\varphi\, x^4+x^8}{1-2x^4+x^8}\, \frac{1-2\cos 2\varphi\, x^8+x^{16}}{1-2x^8+x^{16}}\ldots\ldots$
per $T(\varphi,x)$ erit
1) $T(\varphi,x) = 2A(x^{\frac12}\sin\varphi - x^{\frac92}\sin 3\varphi + x^{\frac{25}{2}}\sin 5\varphi -$ etc.
$A = \frac{\sqrt{\cos v}\sqrt{M\cos v}}{\sqrt{\sin v}} = \frac{[-1+-]{+1-+}2xx+2x^8-2x^{18}}{2(1+2xx+2x^8)(x^{\frac12}+x^{\frac92}+x^{\frac{25}{2}}\ldots)}$
$1+2xx+2x^8+2x^{18}\ldots = \frac{1}{\sqrt{M\cos\varphi}} = \frac{\Pi x^4)^5}{\Pi xx^2\,\Pi x^8)^2}$
$1-2xx+2x^8-2x^{18}\ldots = \frac{\sqrt{\cos\varphi}}{\sqrt{M\cos\varphi}}$ \quad $(pxx)^2+(qx)^2 = 2pxx^2$
$2x^{\frac12}+2x^{\frac92}+2x^{\frac{25}{2}}+$ etc. $= \frac{\sqrt{\sin\varphi}}{\sqrt{M\cos\varphi}}$
